title: Specialized Roubaix SL8 Review: New Future Shock 3, 40mm tyres and more aero

takeaways.text: Future Shock 3 restores home servicing, adds a damping dial from open to locked with five steps and takes different springs; it felt a bit firmer than the previous version.
Clearance of 40 mm beats the Trek Domane's 38 mm and opens up light gravel events.
On 32 mm tires at low pressure it is far smoother than a Tarmac and was calm on wet, muddy roads and short cobbled sections; he left the shock open almost all the time.
He dislikes the Hover bar's high front end and notes Future Shock prevents fully internal routing; it feels slower than an aero endurance bike like the Canyon Endurace.

disclosure: Launch ride; the frame grade and build tested are not stated, so the layup may differ from the Comp's FACT 10r frame.
summary: Two days of launch riding on the Specialized Roubaix SL8 in Portugal, focused on Future Shock 3 and comfort.
